text: {"A": {"fidelity": 4, "omitted": ["tech (to you) in hach chacan tech", "Calam (greatly / vehemently) in Catu Calam yacuntahubaob"], "added": ["and it stops moving as well"], "mistranslated": ["so it moves too (bai û peec xan) -> and it stops moving as well", "nor can He be deceived (maix uchac û tabli) -> and it cannot deceive"]}, "B": {"fidelity": 2, "omitted": ["Ɔocebali tun (Finally / In conclusion)", "t huntenile (forever / perpetually)", "paibentziliix (it is also very necessary)", "y tulacal bahũ baal (and all things [were created]) from the creation clause"], "added": ["of its own", "One day", "as scholars", "<note>The Maya \"hanonexe\" seems to refer to eating; this echoes the old learned view that dreams arise from food and bodily digestion rather than from divine messages.</note>"], "mistranslated": ["the Father existed (paibe t yinhi lay Yumbil) -> the Father was born before", "not created (ma Zihza bilobi) -> not born", "delusions that we imagine when sleeping (û uaiazba hebal c tucliceex â hanonexe) -> only a reflection of what you think about as you eat", "we cannot do this (ma uchac c beticexi) -> This cannot be so for you", "whom we say (c alicexe) -> who, as you say", "our love (c yacunahexe) -> your love", "as we were created (hebicx c Zihzalexe) -> as you were born"]}, "better": "A", "comment": "Translation A is substantially more faithful and correctly preserves Yucatec first-person inclusive grammar and theological nuance, whereas Translation B systematically misinterprets inclusive forms as second-person, commits severe theological errors such as stating God the Father was born, and fabricates a bizarre interpretation of dreams as thoughts while eating."}
